title: Information Set Refinement And Equilibrium
body_html:
Information Set Refinement And Equilibrium

Let $G'$ be obtained from a finite perfect-recall extensive game $G$ by refining some information sets. If $\sigma$ is a pure Nash equilibrium of $G$ and there are no chance moves, then $\sigma$ is also a Nash equilibrium of $G'$.

The conclusion does not extend to mixed equilibria or to games with chance moves. MFoGT gives two counterexamples: matching pennies in extensive form after player 2 observes player 1's move, and a variant where player 1 is replaced by Nature.
proof_html:
Sketch

A pure strategy profile without chance moves induces a unique play. Any profitable deviation at a reached refined information set would also be a profitable deviation in the coarser game.

References

  • [MFoGT, Exercise 6.8.5 and Hints for Chapter 6, Exercise 5] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory. Pure no-chance equilibria survive information-set refinement; mixed or chance cases need not.
